short: Britain's greatest naval commander, whose victory at Trafalgar secured maritime supremacy.
full:
Horatio Nelson rose through the ranks of the Royal Navy during a period of relentless global conflict, distinguished by his daring tactical brilliance and willingness to disobey orthodox orders. He lost the sight in his right eye at Calvi and his right arm at Santa Cruz de Tenerife, yet continued to lead fleets to decisive victories against the French and their allies, most notably at the Battle of the Nile in 1798.

His final and most famous engagement came on 21 October 1805 at the Battle of Trafalgar, where his fleet annihilated the combined French and Spanish forces. Nelson was mortally wounded by a sniper's musket ball during the action, dying just as the scale of his victory became clear. The triumph permanently ended the threat of a Napoleonic invasion and established a century of British naval dominance.
